subject: DPA onboarding: confirmation of transfer mechanisms, subprocessors, and execution mode
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finova.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: DPA request + subprocessors and transfer path questions

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Finova is excited to move to a security review and get the DPA in place so we can start the pilot. Legal asked me to confirm a few items up front so we can route the DPA to procurement quickly:

1) Subprocessor list: can you confirm current subprocessors (analytics, logging, monitoring, cloud infra) and whether Redwood uses any third-party model providers that might access customer data?
2) Transfers: our data protection team wants to confirm how EU-personal-data flows to the US are covered (SCCs, adequacy, or other).
3) Execution: Finova prefers DocuSign for rapid signature. Are you able to sign via DocuSign or do you require AdobeSign or countersign by PDF?

I've attached the worksheet our legal team uses — we typically send a redline back to your template. If you can share your standard DPA template and confirm the above, I can escalate inside Finova and get procurement moving.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Head of Legal Operations
Finova Payments

Attachment: finova_dpa_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finova.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA request + subprocessors and transfer path questions

Hi Marta — great to hear and thanks for the concise list. Looping in our legal and privacy folks to keep things fast. Answers below and I attached our current DPA template (pdf) for your review.

1) Subprocessors: current list is in the template (Appendix A). High level: cloud infra (AWS), metrics & observability (Datadog), PDF rendering (WeasyPrint), and a small vendor for usage analytics. We do not route customer prompt content to third-party model providers — our hosted catalog is managed and executed within Redwood-owned runtime. When customers use dedicated/private options, customers control model placements.

2) Transfers: For EU-origin data we rely on EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) where applicable, and we maintain a Data Processing Addendum that documents transfer mechanisms. For some customers with dedicated capacity we can support data residency configurations to avoid cross-border transfers.

3) Execution: DocuSign works fine for us; we can also accommodate AdobeSign if your procurement requires it. DocuSign is faster for pilot contracts.

Next steps: Laura, can you confirm we're comfortable with the attached template and whether any commercial redlines affect the DPA execution path? Aditya, can you confirm whether the subprocessors list needs an extra attestation language for Finova (some customers request quarterly notices). Priyom — can you note the preferred e-sign vendor per our account record?

Thanks,

—
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0127

Attachment: REDWOOD_DPA_v3.pdf (template stub)

From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finova.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Finova Legal <legal@finova.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA request + subprocessors and transfer path questions

Sergio — thanks for the quick reply and the template. Legal reviewed and made a handful of redlines focused on:
- Section 4 (subprocessors): asking for a quarterly notification clause and the ability to object within 30 days to new subprocessors that handle personal data
- Section 9 (international transfers): clarifying that SCCs will be applied and asking for confirmation around subprocessors that operate from the US/India
- Section 12 (audit & logging): minor clarifications around access to audit evidence for compliance reviews

I've attached the redline PDF and a short text summary. Our preference is DocuSign for the signature path, but procurement will accept AdobeSign as secondary. Can you confirm Redwood's negotiation stance on the 30-day objection window and whether quarterly notices are operationally feasible?

Regards,
Marta

Attachment: Finova_DPA_redline_20261102.pdf (redline stub)
Attachment: redline_changes_summary.txt (text stub)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T12:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA request + subprocessors and transfer path questions

Sergio / team — reviewed Finova's redlines. Quick summary and recommended routing: 

- Quarterly notification: acceptable operationally if we scope notifications to "material changes to the subprocessor list" rather than every non-substantive change. Proposed language: Redwood will publish updates to the subprocessor registry and notify customers of material additions; customers will have 30 days to object to a material addition that processes personal data.

- 30-day objection: acceptable but we should preserve the ability to provide a compatible alternative or continue processing under our standard safeguards if objection is unreasonable. We should propose a cure period and alternative subprocessors where possible.

- SCCs and transfers: we confirm SCCs are the default mechanism for EU transfers. For subprocessors in India/US we will execute SCCs and maintain necessary records; for customers requiring stricter control we can propose a dedicated or private deployment to avoid cross-border transfers.

- Audit evidence: we can provide SOC2 reports and scoped evidence; for ad hoc audit requests we recommend using the Redwood compliance portal and executing an NDA/PA as needed.

Sergio — I recommend sending the marked-up DPA back with the proposed edits and offering DocuSign as the signing method. Priyom — please confirm we have DocuSign envelope templates for DPAs (and record which pipeline this counts against for reporting).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
